 Order

This first bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.421/2023 registered at Police Station City Kotwali, District Bhind (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 366-A, 376 of the IPC and Section 5/6 of the POCSO Act and Sections 3(1)(w)(ii), 3(2)(va) of the SC/ST Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 15/01/2024.
As per the case of prosecution, father of the prosecutrix reported to PS Kotwali, District Bhind that his daughter, aged around 17 years is missing since 10/10/2023.

sentences.text: Victim was recovered from Mangolpuri, Delhi.
In her statement recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C, victim stated that she had love affair with Prashant.
Earlier also, she went to Delhi alongwith Prashant but after three days, her parents brought her back.
On 10/10/2023, she left her home and went to Delhi alongwith Prashant.
They hired a room at Mangolpuri, Delhi.
Both of them were working in shoes factory.
They married at Delhi and started living as husband and wife.
She got pregnant.
On 14/01/2024, her father came to Delhi with police force of PS Kotwali, District Bhind and brought her back.
She desires to live with Prashant.
Statement of victim was also recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
Applicant was arrested on 15/01/2024, he is in custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, Final Report was submitted on 07/02/2024.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant is aged 22 years.
He is labourer by profession.
Applicant has falsely been implicated in this matter under pressure of family members of the victim.
Applicant and victim have married after attaining age of majority.
It is a case of romantic relationship between two young persons.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the applicant as well as victim who still desires to live with applicant.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and cites criminal history of two cases against the applicant.

In reply, learned counsel for the applicant submits that other case under Sections 363 and 366 of the IPC relates to same victim who left her parental home to live with applicant on earlier occasion also.
Another matter relates to offence punishable under Section 34 of the M.P. Excise Act wherein applicant was sentenced to fine.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
